correctness.rationale: An orientation of the complete-bipartite graph is determined uniquely by its alternating labeled same-class runs; there are exactly product(run-factorials) total orders compatible with it. Isotropic Gaussian objective coordinates induce a uniform random rank order, so cone angle is compatible-order-count divided by (p+q)!. Labeled block multiplicity times angle squared yields the formal F(x)F(y)(2+F(x)+F(y))/(1-F(x)F(y)) coefficient. Positive-composition sums with at least two blocks are O(1/p), proved using reciprocal-binomial sums and a merge inequality. One large-class block yields the exact inverse-binomial constant H_q, hence the fixed-q asymptotic. Minimum and maximum follow from factorial balancing. The embedded checker enumerated all orientations for 15 small parameter pairs, comparing exact independent formulas, plus nine large-side coefficient evaluations; analytical arguments establish infinite scope.

originality.rationale: The new two-independent-objective collision probability and fixed-q asymptotic are not entailed by cited normal-fan definitions, prior maximum-linear-extension results, or existing unweighted acyclic-orientation counts. General Gaussian zonotope-vertex sampling work supplies the motivating probability measure but not this bipartite quadratic-angle coefficient or asymptotic; no covering statement was found in the searched records and material inspected. Global novelty is not guaranteed, especially under lonesum-matrix or linear-extension collision terminology. The maximum-angle corollary is explicitly prior-covered.
residual_risks: A quadratic-weighted lonesum matrix identity or second-moment linear-extension result under alternate vocabulary might imply the coefficient without matching keywords.

value.rationale: Repeated random-objective vertex discovery is a natural metric-geometric statistic, and its order-two effective support measures algorithmically meaningful angular concentration. The theorem gives an exact all-size coefficient and a sharp fixed-q limit, showing effective polynomial support of order p^{2q} versus at least (q+1)^p actual distinct vertices. This distribution-wide contrast is not an immediate restatement of the previously known maximum-angle orientation or enumeration formula; it requires a nontrivial full weighted-run summation and quantified multi-run suppression.
